overall_assessment: The actor provenance architecture, staged mode taxonomy, and claim boundary governance implemented across context/claim-boundaries.json, PROJECT_STATUS.md, conductor/frontier-plan.md, conductor/requirements.md (SR-050, SR-093), and docs/maturity/gap-register.md demonstrate outstanding methodological integrity and anti-anthropomorphic discipline. Requirement SR-050 and the frontier plan formalize three distinct operational review modes: Autonomous (initial policy/budget authorization with machine-assessed decisions and draft conclusions; never described as independently human-reviewed), Solo (one human reviewer with configurable uncertainty/conflict queues; machine, human-confirmed, and unresolved decisions remain distinguishable, with fictitious second reviewers strictly barred), and Team (two or more actual people with real reviewer identities, independent/blinded assignments, conflict recording, and explicit adjudication history). Crucially, the non-negotiable rule 'Planned autonomy is not current capability or independently human-reviewed evidence' is upheld: the current runtime enforces human-only final screening exclusions and default-deny external writes, keeping autonomous decision authority explicitly staged. Furthermore, the architecture mandates that multi-agent ensembles cannot count as two independent human reviewers, preserving PRISMA-S and systematic review methodological standards. In PROJECT_STATUS.md, the remote-state reporting policy strictly forbids static documentation from asserting volatile local or GitHub state (such as working tree cleanliness, local/remote branch identity, or open PR counts), requiring these to be evidenced via timestamped receipts. Release risk exceptions are guaranteed full visibility, with documentation-based waivers explicitly denied in docs/maturity/gap-register.md. Deterministic test test_autonomous_solo_and_team_modes_require_actor_provenance confirms that mode provenance rules are locked in governance tests.
verified_invariants: three-mode governance taxonomy: Autonomous, Solo, and Team modes specify distinct authority, human contribution, and required output labeling
anti-anthropomorphic actor provenance: machine decisions must remain clearly attributed to specific models/workers; fictitious human reviewers are strictly barred
ensemble non-equivalence rule: multi-agent ensembles are contractually barred from substituting for independent human reviewer quorums
human-protected runtime default: autonomous final exclusions remain disabled by default, requiring explicit policy and confirmation mechanisms before enablement
reversible mode transitions: transitions between modes preserve historical decision attribution without rewriting history; contested writes use optimistic concurrency
claim boundary enforcement: context/claim-boundaries.json and PROJECT_STATUS.md restrict current status to source-verified technical alpha
volatile remote state exclusion: static prose is barred from asserting volatile branch equality, working-tree cleanliness, or PR state without live receipts
unwaivable exception visibility: release risk exceptions must be recorded with human approval and remain visible in the maturity dossier; documentation waivers are denied

findings.description: Mode definitions, actor provenance policies, and claim boundaries are fully specified and tested in source fixtures; operational deployment of autonomous screening policies and multi-site team trials remain open gates.
findings.recommendation: Preserve open gate 'Implement and evaluate explicit autonomous, solo and team modes; retain current protected defaults until the new policies and actor provenance are tested' until live trial evidence exists.

findings.description: The remote-state reporting policy in PROJECT_STATUS.md eliminates documentation drift by delegating volatile Git and CI status to timestamped snapshot receipts.
findings.recommendation: Maintain enforcement of STALE_STATUS_PHRASES in check_maturity_dossier.py during all future documentation updates.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Staged autonomous, solo, and team modes, actor provenance invariants, anti-anthropomorphism rules, and truthful capability boundaries are verified across specifications and tests.
Premature-claim blocking, volatile state exclusion policy, and exception visibility are strictly enforced by claim boundaries and governance checkers.

limitations: Source-verified mode governance, claim boundaries, and actor provenance framework only; live deployment of autonomous decision policies and multi-site team trials remain open gates.
